newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 25.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Friday's Daily Variety:

* As preparations for the 50th Cannes Film Festival continue, Chinese officials, reportedly angered by the gay theme of "East Palace, West Palace", have confiscated the passport of the film's director Zhang Yuan. Iranian authorities have issued a total ban on "The Taste of Cherry " by Abbas Kiarostami.
* Alec Baldwin has been set opposite Bruce Willis in Universal Pictures' "Simple Simon," sources said.
* The KCBS-TV has been nominated for 18 honors in the Los Angeles Area Emmy Awards, many of them in key news categories.
* There are two key questions about the summer moviegoing season: how big a monster is Universal's "The Lost World", and when will Paramount/Fox's "Titanic" be released to theaters?
* Walt Disney Co has merged its domestic and international homevideo operations and tapped Michael Johnson as president of new division Buena Vista Home Video Worldwide.
* Trimark Pictures has acquired domestic TV and video rights to Cineville and Lakeshore Entertainment's psychological thriller "Casualties," starring Mark Harmon and Caroline Goodall.
* Mike Medavoy's Sony-based Phoenix Pictures is getting ready to film "The Man Who Stole the Mona Lisa," under the direction of Jonathan Darby.
